title: InVideo AI Pricing: Plans and Credit Costs (2026)
summary: InVideo AI pricing costs $20 to $60 monthly depending on the plan.
body_markdown:
## Understand each plan's real cost


For a solo weekly creator or a small business's monthly explainers, Starter covers it, and Plus is where daily posting starts to make sense. Billing cycle moves the bill more than the plan does.


The gap between its paired bars is the point: **annual billing roughly halves the per-video cost** on both paid plans.


If you fill the plan's allowance with finished videos, the bars hold; a retry-heavy month will cost more than they show.


Each per-video figure below is the plan price divided by the videos you make in a month, checked against the credits those videos can spend. Swap in your own volume and your own measured credits per video.


### InVideo AI cost for weekly shorts


Weekly shorts means about four videos a month. Starter then works out to[$5.00 per video on monthly billing ($20 ÷ 4) and $2.50 on annual ($10 ÷ 4)](https://invideo.io/pricing/) .


That only fits if each short costs about 100 credits, retries included, because 400 credits ÷ 4 videos is 100.


The annual figure is half the monthly one, so a creator who will still be posting in twelve months pays about 50% less per short for the same plan.


If you're unsure you'll last a year, monthly billing costs you the $2.50 per video that annual saves.


### Monthly explainers for a small business


Here too, Starter is enough. At four explainers a month the per-video range is the same, $5.00 to $2.50. Because explainers go out less often, the cost of a wasted attempt falls harder on you.


When the month holds only a few videos, one regenerated draft is a larger share of the output.


For daily posting by a two-person team, Plus is the plan to price. Daily output means about thirty finished videos a month, so it costs[$2.00 per video monthly ($60 ÷ 30) and $1.00 annual ($30 ÷ 30)](https://invideo.io/pricing/) .


That assumes each video averages about 66 credits, since 2,000 credits ÷ 30 videos is 66. Plus costs less per credit than Starter at both billing cycles.


### Where the next plan up pays for itself


Per credit, Plus beats Starter, $0.03 against $0.05 monthly and $0.015 against $0.025 annually. Per video, it depends on volume: four videos on Plus cost $15 each monthly ($60 ÷ 4), three times Starter's $5. That saving only materialises if you use the larger pool.


Count the videos you publish in a month and add your retries. If that total regularly exceeds what Starter allows, Plus pays for itself. If it stays under, you're paying for headroom you never touch.
